prompt: Most launch rockets are built in stages that are dropped during ascent. Dropping an empty stage helps mainly because:

options.text: The rocket becomes more aerodynamic once it is shorter
The remaining engines no longer work in thinner air without the stage
The rocket no longer has to accelerate the empty fuel tank's mass, so the remaining fuel produces more acceleration
Gravity stops acting on a rocket once the first stage falls away

explanation: Acceleration depends on force divided by mass. Discarding an empty tank removes dead mass, so the thrust of the next stage accelerates a lighter vehicle and the remaining fuel goes much further.
